functions.comment: A signed number with a prefix and a suffix - and nothing at all when the value is zero and mode is 0, which is why the happiness and population panels have blank rows in a quiet season.

functions.name: Ui_NumberToBuffer
functions.signature: void Ui_NumberToBuffer(int value, int start, int forceSign)
functions.comment: Formats value into g_numberBuffer starting at index start, writing '-' or '+' at start and shifting when it does. Callers pass start = 1 so index 0 stays free for a sign character.

functions.name: Ui_DrawCount
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawCount(int value, int unitIndex, int x, int y, void * font, int colour)
functions.comment: A number followed by a noun from L2.eng group 8: index unitIndex when the value is 1 or -1, unitIndex + 1 otherwise. Group 8 is singular at even indices and plural at odd.

functions.name: Ui_DrawHappinessDelta
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawHappinessDelta(int value, int x, int y, void * font, int colourPos, int colourNeg)
functions.comment: Draws a bracketed signed number with the happiness face after it: a bracket, Ui_DrawDelta, g_miscCtySheet frame 0x17, a closing bracket.

functions.name: Ui_DrawUnitNoun
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawUnitNoun(int value, int unitIndex, int x, int y, void * font, int colour)
functions.comment: Just the group 8 noun, singular when the value is 1.

functions.name: Ui_DrawYear
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawYear(int year, int x, int y, int style)
functions.comment: A year with BC or AD from L2.eng group 26. style 3 prints the number alone, which is what the graph axes use.

functions.name: Ui_HistoryGraph
functions.signature: uint Ui_HistoryGraph(int x, int y, int mode)
functions.comment: The 402x155 history graph on the population and happiness panels. mode 0 reads g_countyHistory +0x00 (population, u32), mode 1 reads +0x04 (happiness, u8), walking g_historyLength turns from g_historyHead and wrapping at 400. Returns the peak, which the caller prints. Background from graphs.pl8.

functions.name: Res_LoadStatic
functions.comment: Loads the thirteen records of g_preloadTable into their fixed .data buffers - three palettes, five fonts, mouse.pl8, System2.pl8, Panels.pl8, l2.eng and vill_gd8.pl8. That table is the whole interface asset list.

functions.name: Res_LoadButtons
functions.comment: Loads system2.pl8 (skin 0) or system.pl8 (skin 1) into g_systemSheet. Same size and same 84-frame layout, but 69 of System2.pl8s frames are entirely index 0 and none of System.pl8s are, and the kingdom screens ask for skin 1 - so the county panels button art is System.pl8. docs/screens-county.md section 4.2.

functions.name: CountyStrip_Draw
functions.comment: The selected county's strip in the map sidebar: name, population, happiness, tax rate, ration achieved and the health thermometer for an owned county; frame 0x3A and the owner's name for one you do not hold. docs/screens-county.md section 2.

functions.name: CountyStrip_Click
functions.comment: The 2x2 hotspot over the county strip, and the only way to any of the four county panels: x 488..547 / y 182..211 population, x 568..629 / y 182..211 happiness, and the same two columns below y 212 for tax and rations. The dead band 548..567 is where the health thermometer is drawn.

functions.name: CountyStrip_JobClick
functions.comment: The sidebar's lower plate: farm jobs left of x 560, industry right of it. Sets g_jobPanelJob and opens screen 0x0F.

functions.name: Panel_Ration
functions.comment: The ration panel (screen 0x19). Draws L2.eng group 87 against county +0x15E (wanted), +0x15D (achieved, red when they differ), +0x09 (health band), +0x11 and +0x10 as happiness deltas, and the Fed / Eaten rows from +0x16C, +0x170, +0x174, +0x178 and +0x17C.

functions.name: Panel_RationSlider
functions.comment: The grain-to-livestock slider: caps from g_systemSheet frames 0x4A and 0x4B at x 200 and 324, a 100-pixel track from x 224 to 323, and the knob (frame 0x4C, 10 wide) at 220 + county +0x15F.

functions.name: Panel_JobDetail
functions.comment: The job popup (screen 0x0F) for g_jobPanelJob, 1..9 into L2.eng group 74. Draws the worker count with the group 8 noun for job*2 + 30, red when labour +0x00 is below +0x04 and a second colour when it is above +0x08 - which is what shows the labour record to be three integers a job, not one.

functions.name: Panel_JobIndustry
functions.comment: The mining, quarrying, wood and blacksmith bodies of the job popup. Maps jobs 5, 6, 7 and 8 to industry records 1, 3, 0 and 2, the same order the village artwork implies.

functions.name: Panel_JobGrain
functions.comment: The grain body of the job popup: store, fertility band, the event and weather effects on the store, and either what will be sown in spring or what is growing and when it is harvested. Nothing on it is clickable - the player never chooses how much to sow.

functions.name: Panel_JobCattle
functions.comment: The cattle body of the job popup: L2.eng group 77 calf births, cow deaths and the herd-crowding bands.

functions.name: Panel_JobReclamation
functions.comment: The field-reclamation body of the job popup: how many fields are being reclaimed and how many seasons to the next one.

functions.name: Panel_JobBlacksmith
functions.comment: The blacksmith body of the job popup, with smithy.pl8 and hearth.pl8 and the weapon's cost from g_weaponCost.

functions.name: Village_Draw
functions.comment: The village screen (screen 0x02): villani1/villani2/vill.pl8, villtops.pl8, and the weather and fertility lines when Advanced Farming is on. The scene starts at y = g_villageTopY.

functions.name: Village_DrawPeasants
functions.comment: Draws the eight peasant clusters at g_jobClusterOrigins + (0x40, g_villageTopY).

functions.name: Village_DrawCluster
functions.signature: void Village_DrawCluster(int cluster, int x, int y)
functions.comment: One cluster: up to 25 icons from g_peasantIcons at the offsets in g_peasantIconOffsets, each frame bumped by one while the cluster is the drag source.

functions.name: Village_Animate
functions.comment: Steps the village's animation counters and draws the animated overlays.

functions.name: Village_BoxSelect
functions.comment: Marks every peasant icon inside the rubber-band box, and abandons the whole selection if the box reaches into a second cluster. Leaves the cluster in g_villageDragCluster and the count in g_villageDragCount.

functions.name: Village_ClusterAt
functions.comment: Which of the eight clusters the pointer is over, 1-based, or 0.

functions.name: Labour_Move
functions.signature: void Labour_Move(int county, int fromCluster, int toCluster, int workers)
functions.comment: Moves workers between two labour slots of one county and re-runs the county's food and industry passes twice. The caller's count is selected icons times county +0xB8 (popBand), clamped to what the source slot holds - so one icon is one twenty-fifth of the population, rounded up.

functions.name: Job_SlotForCluster
functions.comment: Cluster to labour slot through g_jobClusterToSlot, with cluster 0 overridden from stone (5) to iron (4) when the county has industry 1's resource and not industry 3's. That single case pins industry 1 = iron and industry 3 = stone.

functions.name: Village_RebuildIcons
functions.comment: Rebuilds g_peasantIcons for one county: workers divided by popBand icons per cluster, with the surplus or shortfall against the slot's +0x04 and +0x08 drawn in a different frame.

functions.name: Tax_Increase
functions.comment: The tax panel's up arrow. Guards taxRate < 0x32 - the player's tax ceiling is 50, and this is where it lives.

functions.name: Tax_IncreaseCounty
functions.comment: Raises one county's tax rate by one, capped at 50, then Tax_RecomputePreview and a redraw.

functions.name: Tax_Decrease
functions.comment: The tax panel's down arrow. Guards taxRate != 0.

functions.name: Tax_DecreaseCounty
functions.comment: Lowers one county's tax rate by one, floored at 0.

functions.name: Tax_RecomputePreview
functions.comment: Recomputes one county's tax display: +0xC0 taxShown from population, the castle multiplier and the rate; +0x0F = 5 - rate; and +0x16 from g_taxHappinessOther[rate]. It is the only writer of +0x16 anywhere in the binary, so the empire tax happiness term is a table lookup rather than 5 - rate.

functions.name: Panels_RefreshAll
functions.comment: End of the season pipeline: Ration_Apply, the next-season preview and Tax_RecomputePreview for every county. This is the second Ration_Apply call docs/decisions.md C20 identified from the save.

functions.name: Ration_Increase
functions.comment: The ration panel's up arrow. Guards rationWanted < 5.

functions.name: Ration_IncreaseCounty
functions.comment: Raises one county's wanted ration by one, capped at 5, then re-applies rations and redraws.

functions.name: Ration_Decrease
functions.comment: The ration panel's down arrow. Guards rationWanted > 0.

functions.name: Ration_DecreaseCounty
functions.comment: Lowers one county's wanted ration by one, floored at 0.

functions.name: Ration_SliderClick
functions.comment: The grain-to-livestock slider's hit test: (200,220,24,24) steps down, (325,220,24,24) steps up, and (224,220,102,24) jumps to mouseX - 224. Clamped 0..100, and refused outright unless the county's owner is g_localPlayer.

functions.name: Ration_SetSplit
functions.signature: void Ration_SetSplit(int county, int split, int sweep)
functions.comment: Sets county +0x15F and re-runs the food pass; if the new split changes nothing it walks back towards the old value looking for one that does.

functions.name: Panel_OpenRation
functions.comment: Opens the ration panel (screen 0x19).

functions.name: Panel_OpenPopulation
functions.comment: Opens the population panel (screen 0x14).

functions.name: Panel_OpenHappiness
functions.comment: Opens the happiness panel (screen 0x16).

functions.name: Panel_OpenTax
functions.comment: Opens the tax panel (screen 0x15).

functions.name: Turn_End
functions.comment: The sidebar's full-width bottom button: ends the local player's turn by writing 999 into the realm record's +0x00.

functions.name: Sidebar_Button
functions.comment: The five buttons in the 162x30 strip at y 430, on g_uiHotspotId 1..5: the county's army (screen 0x17), the court (screen 0x09), send supplies (screen 0x18), and two more.

functions.name: Court_Draw
functions.comment: The court screen (0x09): L2.eng group 70 against the realm record - gold +0x118, iron +0x120, stone +0x128, wood +0x130, six weapon stocks from +0x140, army wages +0xFC and expected tax +0x15C.

functions.name: Field_SetType
functions.signature: void Field_SetType(uint county, int tile, int brush)
functions.comment: Repaints one map tile's field type for a county and re-runs its food passes. Called from a map click with the brush in g_uiHotspotId; this, not any county panel, is how fields are assigned.

globals.name: g_clipState
globals.comment: Clip state: 0 unclipped, 1 clipped left, 2 clipped right, 5 fully offscreen.

globals.name: g_clipVisibleWidth
globals.comment: Visible (clipped) sprite width.

globals.name: g_clipSrcSkip
globals.comment: Source bytes skipped per row = width - visible width.

globals.name: g_clipDstAdvance
globals.comment: Destination advance per row = screen stride - visible width.

globals.name: g_spriteWidth
globals.comment: Current sprite width.

globals.name: g_spriteHeight
globals.comment: Current sprite height.

globals.name: g_spriteDataOffset
globals.comment: Current source data offset within the PL8 buffer.

globals.name: g_screenStride
globals.comment: Screen stride, 640.

globals.name: g_blitRowCount
globals.comment: Blitter row counter. Not frame-record byte 0x0D - Clip_Vertical overwrites it before every blit, so the byte-0x0D load in Pl8_DrawFrame is dead.

globals.name: g_ddrawInterface
globals.comment: A DirectDraw interface pointer. It was NULL at the crash at 0x004522B5, which happened when the window was deactivated during startup under DxWnd.

globals.name: g_resourceTable
globals.comment: The game's resource directory: {char name[16]; u32 size;} records. Entries 0-31 are the map tile sets, eight layers x four seasons; 32-63 the zoom-2 sets; 64+ the battle-map sets. See docs/formats/maps-layers.md 1.1.

globals.name: g_scenarioIndex
globals.comment: The map slot, 0..59, used unshifted. Map_LoadLattice seeks slot * 0x80C1 (the whole slot stride), Eng_DrawString(101, g_scenarioIndex) indexes the 60 slot names in L2.eng group 101, and Minimap_Load takes the MAPnn.PL8 file from slot >> 2 and one of its four slots from slot & 3. An earlier note here said the low 2 bits select the season variant of the tile set: they do not - Gfx_LoadCountyMode takes the season from g_season.

globals.name: g_tiles
globals.comment: Runtime tile array, 4096 records x 8 bytes, index y*64 + x. +1 plane0 flags, +2 bank, +3 frame, +4 plane3, +5 unit index on this tile, +6 saved terrain frame, +7 county. See docs/formats/maps-layers.md 5.3.

globals.name: g_screenLattice
globals.comment: Runtime 129x65 dword screen lattice, row stride 0x104. Covered cells hold tileIndex*8; uncovered cells keep 0x0FFF0000 + backgroundFrame.

globals.name: g_countyCount
globals.comment: Highest county id on the loaded map, i.e. the county count. Set by Map_LoadPlanes as max(plane5) over ids below 0x11.

globals.name: g_units
globals.comment: Unit array, 150 records x 0x1A4 bytes, index 1..149 (0 unused). +0x00 owner, +0x08 type, +0x0A/+0x0B tile x/y, +0x0C tile offset, +0x10 county, +0x14..+0x17 destination x/y, +0x14F merchant route index, +0x150 'needs a destination', +0x151 destination county, +0x164 merchant route cursor, +0x16C.. cargo.

globals.name: g_lastUnitIndex
globals.comment: Index of the unit Unit_Spawn just allocated. Callers read it straight after the call to fill in the rest of the record.

globals.name: g_foundTileX
globals.comment: X of the tile the last Map_FindFree*TileNear search settled on.

globals.name: g_foundTileY
globals.comment: Y of the tile the last Map_FindFree*TileNear search settled on.

globals.name: g_merchantRoutes
globals.comment: The six merchant trade routes: 6 rows x 16 county ids, built from plane 4 on castle tiles. Row n is the itinerary of the merchant named by L2.eng group 5 string n. See docs/formats/plane4.md.

globals.name: g_merchantStartCounty
globals.comment: Six bytes: the county each merchant starts in, chosen by Merchant_PickStartCounties. A zero entry stops Merchant_SpawnAll.

globals.name: g_merchantCount
globals.comment: Number of merchants Merchant_SpawnAll actually placed, 1..6.

globals.name: g_playerStartTable
globals.comment: Player start table, {county, slot} byte pairs indexed by the plane-4 value on a settlement tile. See docs/formats/maps-layers.md 5.1.

globals.name: g_playerStartCount
globals.comment: Number of non-zero player start slots on the loaded map: 5, 4 or 2 across the shipped maps.

globals.name: g_county0_anchorX
globals.comment: X of county 0's anchor tile in the county record array (stride 0x300); County_FindFreeRoadTile searches around county*0x300 + this.

globals.name: g_county0_anchorY
globals.comment: Y of county 0's anchor tile, as above.

globals.name: g_turnPhase
globals.comment: Turn state machine phase, switched on by FUN_0049a010. Phase 6 step 1 is Merchant_AdvanceAll.

globals.name: g_turnPhaseStep
globals.comment: Step counter within the current turn phase; incremented on every FUN_0049a010 call.

globals.name: g_battleMen
globals.comment: Battle figure array, 80 records of 0x1B0 bytes, index 1..80 (0 unused). A figure is one drawn man representing g_menPerFigure real soldiers. +0x09 selected, +0x12 troop type, +0x13 owner is human, +0x18 facing 0..7, +0x1C cell byte offset, +0x20/+0x22 x,y, +0x24/+0x26 target x,y, +0x2C owner (0 = free slot), +0x31 state, +0x172 armour, +0x174 target figure, +0x178 owning unit, +0x17A side, +0x17E melee opponent, +0x189 move delay, +0x18B melee recovery interval, +0x197 strength band, +0x198 heavy-blow bonus, +0x19A hits, +0x19C melee attack, +0x1A0 men left. Full map in docs/battle.md.

globals.name: g_battleUnits
globals.comment: Battle unit array, 80 records of 0x34 bytes, index 1..80 (0 unused). A unit is what the player selects and orders. +0x00 owner (0 = free slot), +0x01 human controlled, +0x02 figure count, +0x03 side (0 or 4), +0x04/+0x06 first and last figure index, +0x08 category, +0x0F firing timer, +0x14 re-target countdown, +0x1A orders, +0x1E/+0x20 position, +0x22/+0x24 target, +0x2C ordered target figure, +0x30 target cell offset.

globals.name: g_missiles
globals.comment: Missile / effect array, 100 records of 0x4C bytes, index 1..100. +0x06 firing figure, +0x08 owner, +0x09 class (1 bow, 2 crossbow, 3 catapult, 5 fire, 7 falling figure), +0x0A/+0x0C position in 1/32 cell, +0x14/+0x16 cell x,y, +0x1C cell byte offset, +0x2F launch elevation, +0x36 distance flown, +0x38 range, +0x40 power.

globals.name: g_battlefield
globals.comment: Battlefield cell array, 80x80 records of 8 bytes, index (y*80 + x)*8. +0 terrain id, +1 flags (0x10 and 0x80 impassable), +2 flags, +3 graphic index, +4 elevation, +5 index of the figure standing here, +6 head of the missile list in this cell, +7 surface type (7 bridge, 10 and 17 burning, 15 woodland).

globals.name: g_curBattleMan
globals.comment: Index of the figure currently being updated. The whole figure state machine reads its subject from this global rather than from a parameter.

globals.name: g_otherBattleMan
globals.comment: Index of the other figure in the current interaction: the melee opponent, the missile target, or the figure being swapped with.

globals.name: g_curBattleUnit
globals.comment: Index of the unit currently being updated by Battle_UpdateAllUnits.

globals.name: g_lastBattleMan
globals.comment: Index of the figure BattleMan_Create just allocated.

globals.name: g_lastBattleUnit
globals.comment: Index of the unit BattleUnit_Alloc just allocated.

globals.name: g_lastMissile
globals.comment: Index of the missile Missile_Spawn just allocated.

globals.name: g_curMissile
globals.comment: Index of the missile Missile_Step is advancing.

globals.name: g_battleSizeClass
globals.comment: Battlefield size class 0..8, from the combined army size. It selects g_menPerFigure, the strength-band thresholds, and the burning-damage rate.

globals.name: g_menPerFigure
globals.comment: How many real soldiers one drawn figure stands for: 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512 or 1024 by size class. Reduced for a small army so that a side always gets at least 9 figures.

globals.name: g_battleIsSiege
globals.comment: Non-zero for a siege: selects the castle battlefield builder, the siege unit-order tables and Battle_RaiseSideSiege.

globals.name: g_localPlayer
globals.comment: The player index this machine controls. Compared against a unit owner to decide whose units are on the player side.

globals.name: g_strengthBand1
globals.comment: Men in a figure below which it drops to strength band 1 - 75% of a full figure.

globals.name: g_strengthBand2
globals.comment: Band 2 threshold - 50% of a full figure.

globals.name: g_strengthBand3
globals.comment: Band 3 threshold - about 19-25% of a full figure.

globals.name: g_absDx
globals.comment: Absolute x distance left by Dist_Manhattan / Dist_Chebyshev.

globals.name: g_absDy
globals.comment: Absolute y distance left by Dist_Manhattan / Dist_Chebyshev.

globals.name: g_troopStrengthWeight
globals.comment: Seven ints, the autocalc strength weight of one soldier by troop type: peasant 2, crossbowman 16, maceman 8, swordsman 13, pikeman 9, archer 13, knight 22. Used only for army strength comparisons, not by the real-time battle.

globals.name: g_troopBattleStats
globals.comment: Per troop type, 11 rows of 5 ints: max figures per unit, cell footprint, max figures per formation row, weapon class (index into g_missileStats), move delay in ticks.

globals.name: g_missileStats
globals.comment: Per weapon class, 4 rows of 5 ints: range in 1/8 cells, reload interval in ticks, sub-steps per tick, damage, sprite-bank offset. Class 0 melee (all zero), 1 bow (120, 50, 4, 50, 0), 2 crossbow (64, 100, 4, 200, 8), 3 catapult (160, 100, 4, 200, 16).

globals.name: g_meleeAttackTable
globals.comment: Melee attack value by troop type and strength band, 11 rows of 4 shorts. Peasant/crossbow/archer 5,4,3,2; mace and sword 15,12,10,6; pike 10,8,6,5; knight 20,15,11,6; siege engines all zero.

globals.name: g_menPerFigureTable
globals.comment: Nine ints indexed by battlefield size class: 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024 men per drawn figure.

globals.name: g_sizeClassLadder
globals.comment: Eight (threshold, size class) pairs mapping total men to the battlefield size class: 305, 609, 1217, 2433, 4865, 9729, 19457, 38913, then 8.

globals.name: g_siegeScaleLadder
globals.comment: Eight (threshold, value) pairs giving how many men one siege engine counts as when choosing the size class.

globals.name: g_strengthBandTable
globals.comment: Three ints per battlefield size class: the men-per-figure thresholds for strength bands 1, 2 and 3 - 75%, 50% and about 19-25% of a full figure.

globals.name: g_raiseOrder
globals.comment: The order in which troop types become units in a field battle: ram, oil, knight, sword, mace, pike, crossbow, archer, peasant, tower, catapult.

globals.name: g_raiseOrderSiege
globals.comment: The castle-defender raise order, eight troop types: oil, archer, crossbow, knight, peasant, sword, mace, pike. Catapults, towers and rams are absent.

globals.name: g_troopTickTable
globals.comment: Eleven function pointers indexed by troop type. Each reloads that troop per-tick constants - animation set, recovery interval, heavy-blow bonus, armour - and then tail-calls g_manStateTable[state].

globals.name: g_manStateTable
globals.comment: Eighteen figure-state handlers indexed by figure byte +0x31. Known: 2 dead, 4 melee, 5 idle/firing, 6 blocked, 7 look for melee, 12 siege engine attacking, 17 closing to attack.

globals.name: g_unitOrderTableField
globals.comment: Five unit order handlers for a field battle, indexed by unit category 0..4.

globals.name: g_unitOrderTableSiegeAtt
globals.comment: Nine unit order handlers for the siege attacker (unit side non-zero), indexed by unit category 0..8.

globals.name: g_unitOrderTableSiegeDef
globals.comment: Eleven unit order handlers for the siege defender (unit side zero), indexed by unit category 0..10.

globals.name: g_cellNeighbourOffsets
globals.comment: Eight ints, the battlefield cell byte offsets of the neighbours in direction order 0..7: -0x280, -0x278, +8, +0x288, +0x280, +0x278, -8, -0x288.

globals.name: g_troopsTable
globals.comment: The parsed TROOPS*.ENG table: short[35][2][5][11], row stride 0xDC, side stride 0x6E, difficulty stride 0x16. See docs/formats/eng.md and the correction in docs/battle.md.

globals.name: g_troopsAdvantage
globals.comment: The per-battle defensive advantage 0..10, one per TROOPS*.ENG row.

globals.name: g_troopsRowBase
globals.comment: Four ints, 0/10/20/35: the first g_troopsTable row for each battle category.

globals.name: g_battleArmyA
globals.comment: Index into g_units of the first army in the current battle. It is raised on side 4.

globals.name: g_battleArmyB
globals.comment: Index into g_units of the second army. It is raised on side 0, and is the side the castle-defender path is applied to in a siege.

globals.name: g_battleStrengthA
globals.comment: Autocalc strength of army A: sum of count[t] * g_troopStrengthWeight[t] over troop types 0..6.

globals.name: g_battleStrengthB
globals.comment: Autocalc strength of army B.

globals.name: g_debugSelectedMan
globals.comment: The figure index BattleDebug_Panel prints.

globals.name: g_pathCost
globals.comment: Pathfinder cost field, u16 per battlefield cell, index y*80 + x. 0 means unvisited, 1 the start cell, 998 (0x3E6) blocked.

globals.name: g_pathQueue
globals.comment: Pathfinder frontier, a circular queue of 0x1900 cell indices with head g_pathQueueHead and tail g_pathQueueTail.

globals.name: g_pathQueueHead
globals.comment: Read cursor of g_pathQueue.

globals.name: g_pathQueueTail
globals.comment: Write cursor of g_pathQueue; wraps at 0x1900.

globals.name: g_pathStepCost
globals.comment: Per-cell step cost the flood fill charges: a cell is only expanded once it has been reached this many times.

globals.name: g_pathVisitCount
globals.comment: How many times the flood fill has reached each cell, compared against g_pathStepCost.

globals.name: g_pathElevation
globals.comment: Per-cell elevation the flood fill and Path_Extract read; a step is only allowed between cells differing by at most 1.

globals.name: g_pathWaypoints
globals.comment: Scratch route built by Path_Extract: (x, y) byte pairs, at most 150, ordered destination-first. BattleMan_SetPath copies it into the figure.

globals.name: g_cellIndexNeighbours
globals.comment: Eight ints, the battlefield cell-index (not byte) deltas in direction order 0..7: -0x50, -0x4F, +1, +0x51, +0x50, +0x4F, -1, -0x51.

globals.name: g_counties
globals.comment: The county array: 17 records of 0x300 bytes, index 1..16 (0 unused). Base, count and stride all appear together in the multiplayer sync descriptor at 0x004D5B10 and in the save-block table at 0x004DE960.

globals.name: g_realms
globals.comment: Realm/player array: 6 records of 0x160 bytes, index 1..5. +0x00 AI step, +0x04 in play, +0x05 human, +0x07 lord, +0x28 empire tax happiness, +0x2B rank, +0x50 score, +0xFC army wages, +0x118 gold.

globals.name: g_countyFieldTiles
globals.comment: 17 x 20 u32 tile indices - the map tiles that are this county's farm fields. Save block 12 is exactly 1360 bytes = 17 * 80.

globals.name: g_saveBlocks
globals.comment: 225 {u32 address, u32 length} records terminated by a zero length; Save_Write dumps each in order. Sums to 267,028 bytes.

globals.name: g_syncBlocks
globals.comment: Seven 12-byte {count, stride, firstComparedOffset} descriptors used by Sync_CompareState and Sync_Checksum: counties (17, 0x300, 5), realms (6, 0x160, 6), units (151, 0x1A4, 0), battle men (81, 0x1B0, 18), missiles (101, 0x4C, 4), battle units (81, 0x34, 0).

globals.name: g_stateArrayPtrs
globals.comment: Eight pointers in the same order as g_syncBlocks: counties, counties, realms, units, battle men, missiles, battle units, battlefield. No reader was found; it corroborates every base address.

globals.name: g_season
globals.comment: Current season 1..4, used directly as the index into L2.eng group 29 (Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter). Season_Advance sets it before running the economy, so the economy sees the season being entered.

globals.name: g_seasonNext
globals.comment: The season after g_season; the year rolls when the season that just ended was 4.

globals.name: g_seasonPrev
globals.comment: The previous value of g_season.

globals.name: g_year
globals.comment: Displayed year. 1268 on turn 1.

globals.name: g_yearNext
globals.comment: g_year + 1, staged for the next roll.

globals.name: g_turnCount
globals.comment: Turns elapsed; divides the happiness accumulator to give the running average.

globals.name: g_selectedCounty
globals.comment: The county the county panels display.

globals.name: g_weatherCounty
globals.comment: The county picked this season for the doubled local weather swing.

globals.name: g_optDifficulty
globals.comment: New-game difficulty 0..3 (easy/normal/hard/impossible, L2.eng group 103 indices 11..14). Scales AI gold, AI free resources and AI army wages.

globals.name: g_optAdvancedFarming
globals.comment: Advanced Farming (L2.eng group 102 index 0). When 0, weather is forced to Cloudy in every county and fertility is forced to 0.

globals.name: g_optArmiesEat
globals.comment: Armies Eat (L2.eng group 102 index 3). When 1, garrison and enemy troop counts are added to the county's food requirement.

globals.name: g_optTimeLimit
globals.comment: Turn time limit in seconds, 0 for none.

globals.name: g_grainYieldPerSack
globals.comment: 12. "Each sack planted will grow into 12 sacks" - the game's own FAQ text, L2.eng group 292 index 4.

globals.name: g_grainMaxSacksPerField
globals.comment: 10. The top of Grain_Sow's descending search; the manual's "up to 5 sacks" is wrong.

globals.name: g_grainLabourDivisorAdv
globals.comment: 5. Labour divisor used when Advanced Farming is on.

globals.name: g_grainLabourDivisor
globals.comment: 2. Labour divisor used when Advanced Farming is off.

globals.name: g_dairyPerHead
globals.comment: 5. People fed per head of the standing herd, without slaughter.

globals.name: g_foodPerHead
globals.comment: 10. People fed by one slaughtered animal.

globals.name: g_foodPerSack
globals.comment: 6. People fed by one sack of grain.

globals.name: g_birthRateLadder
globals.comment: 20 {population, percent} pairs from (40, 100) down to (3000, 1): the base birth rate falls as a county fills up.

globals.name: g_deathRateByHealth
globals.comment: Percent per season by health band 0..4: 35, 20, 8, 3, 0.

globals.name: g_deathRateBySeason
globals.comment: Percent per season, indexed 1..4: Spring 4, Summer 0, Autumn 2, Winter 8.

globals.name: g_healthDeltaTable
globals.comment: int[6][5]: change to the health meter by ration level 0..5 and health band 0..4. Row 3 (Normal) is the first that is positive.

globals.name: g_healthBandLadder
globals.comment: Five {threshold, band} pairs: 10/0, 35/1, 65/2, 90/3, 100/4.

globals.name: g_healthHappiness
globals.comment: Happiness per season by health band: -10, -5, 0, +1, +2 for Diseased, Sick, Average, Good, Perfect (L2.eng group 20).

globals.name: g_herdWeatherPct
globals.comment: Percent change to the herd by weather 0..5: Frost -2, Drought -10, Sunny +5, Cloudy 0, Storms -5, Flooding -10.

globals.name: g_rationTable
globals.comment: Six {divisor, multiplier} pairs: (1,0) None, (4,1) Quarter, (2,1) Half, (1,1) Normal, (1,2) Double, (1,3) Triple - exactly L2.eng group 21.

globals.name: g_eventTable
globals.comment: The random-event id ring Event_RollAll draws from; 0 means no event.

globals.name: g_armyHappinessCost
globals.comment: int[102] happiness cost of raising an army, indexed by the PERCENTAGE of the county's population taken rather than by the number of men: 0, 1, 1, 1, 2 ... 90 at half the county, then a flat 101 from index 61 up. FUN_004A5003 reads it unbounded, so a county under 50 people indexes past the end into g_goodsPrice and gets a free army. 0x004D8778 + 102 * 4 is exactly 0x004D8910, which is what fixes the length.

globals.name: g_goodsPrice
globals.comment: Merchant base price per good id, 15 entries in L2.eng group 6 order: -, grain 2, cattle 12, sheep 0, ale 1, wool 0, iron 1, stone 2, timber 1, pikes 13, bows 16, maces 10, crossbows 24, swords 23, mail 44.

globals.name: g_goodsStock
globals.comment: A second 15-entry table on the same good ids: 1000 grain, 100 cattle, 200 sheep, 100 ale, 500 wool, 100 iron, 100 stone, 200 timber, 500 each weapon. Reads like the quantity a merchant carries.

globals.name: g_weaponCost
globals.comment: Six {wood, iron} pairs: crossbow 6/10, mace 4/4, sword 3/10, pike 6/3, bow 13/0, armour 4/18. Debited by Industry_Produce.

globals.name: g_castleMaterial
globals.comment: Five {wood, stone} pairs: palisade 400/40, motte and bailey 800/80, Norman keep 200/1000, stone castle 400/2000, royal castle 800/3000.

globals.name: g_castleWorkforce
globals.comment: Man-seasons per castle type, each value stored twice: 200, 400, 800, 1500, 2500.

globals.name: g_castleGarrisonCap
globals.comment: Troops a castle can hold: 150, 200, 200, 400, 600.

globals.name: g_castleTaxBonus
globals.comment: Percent tax bonus by castle type: 50, 75, 100, 125, 150 - the same ratios as Tax_CollectAll's 480/560/640/720/800 over the castle-less 320.

globals.name: g_castleFreeArchers
globals.comment: Archers a newly finished castle is given: 50, 150, 150, 200, 300.

globals.name: g_aiPersonality
globals.comment: Per-AI-lord behaviour parameters, three 0x50-byte rows per lord and only the first row used, so the stride is 0xF0. THIS ADDRESS IS THE RECORD'S +0x04 FIELD, not its start: AI_SetTaxRates reads *(int *)(&g_aiPersonality + (lord * 3 - 3) * 0x50) as the tax-ladder selector, and the record itself begins four bytes earlier at 0x004D8A58 with the farming style AI_ManageFields dispatches on. Four records, lords 1..4: farming style 1/1/0/9, tax ladder 2/2/2/1. A fifth would begin at 0x004D8E18 and what is there fits no pattern.

globals.name: g_aiGoldGrant
globals.comment: int[5][4] free gold per turn by AI lord and difficulty for a realm holding three or more counties: 0/0/0/0, 0/400/700/1200, 100/500/800/1400, 0/400/700/1200, 250/600/1100/1800.

globals.name: g_aiGoldGrantSmall
globals.comment: The same shape, used when the realm holds fewer than three counties.

globals.name: g_aiStrengthAdvantage
globals.comment: The AI's view of the battle, recomputed every 101 frames by Battle_UpdateStrengthAdvantage: weighted AI men as a percentage of weighted human men, minus 100, plus a -10..+21 jitter outside deterministic play. Every field and siege handler branches on it. It is one global for the whole battle, not per side and not per unit.

globals.name: g_aiAggressionThreshold
globals.comment: Set to 5 by Rules_InitConstants and read only by the three field order handlers: above this advantage they attack, at or below it they hold and skirmish.

globals.name: g_aiSortieThreshold
globals.comment: Set to 260 by Rules_InitConstants and read only by the four siege-defender handlers: above this advantage the garrison lays the drawbridge patch and charges out.

globals.name: g_aiAdvantageTimer
globals.comment: Frame counter in Battle_UpdateAllUnits; at 101 it triggers Battle_UpdateStrengthAdvantage and resets.

globals.name: g_aiCommitCounter
globals.comment: Zeroed by Battle_Start. A field melee handler adds 3 when the side's engagement count passes its budget byte and 20 when the AI's missile troops fall below an eighth of its army; every unengaged melee unit counts it down by 1 per think. While it is non-zero every AI melee unit goes into free pursuit and every missile unit closes half the distance, so it is a commitment counter rather than a hold.

globals.name: g_aiRallyRequest
globals.comment: Raised by a field melee handler that is under attack, together with g_aiRallyX / g_aiRallyY; the field missile handler consumes it and shifts two cells toward that point. The only unit-to-unit signal in the battle AI.

globals.name: g_aiRallyX
globals.comment: X of the enemy unit that attacked the melee unit which raised g_aiRallyRequest.

globals.name: g_aiRallyY
globals.comment: Y of the enemy unit that attacked the melee unit which raised g_aiRallyRequest.

globals.name: g_aiEngagementCount
globals.comment: Counts, since Battle_Start, how many times a field melee handler has thought while its unit had a live attacker. Compared against the per-battlefield budget byte at 0x00553080 to decide whether the side should commit.

globals.name: g_aiMenTotal
globals.comment: Surviving men over all figures whose owner is not human, from Battle_CountMenByType.

globals.name: g_aiMenMissile
globals.comment: Surviving crossbowmen plus archers on the non-human side. When this falls below an eighth of g_aiMenTotal the field melee handlers add 20 to g_aiCommitCounter.

globals.name: g_aiMenKnight
globals.comment: Surviving knights on the non-human side. Two siege-attacker handlers compare it against g_aiMenTotal.

globals.name: g_battlePhase
globals.comment: Set to 2 by Battle_Start. BattleUnits_RebuildFromFigures does nothing unless it holds 2.

globals.name: g_battleUnitCount
globals.comment: Number of occupied unit slots, recounted at the end of every BattleUnits_RebuildFromFigures pass.

globals.name: g_battleApproachLane
globals.comment: 0..3, chosen at random by Battle_Start in normal play and advanced cyclically in deterministic play. Selects which of four columns of the castle approach tables the siege attackers use, and which end-of-field slot the field handlers march to.

globals.name: g_battleRallyGroup
globals.comment: 0 or 1, chosen the same way as g_battleApproachLane. Selects which group of three rally waypoints the field handlers use.

globals.name: g_rallyWaypoints
globals.comment: The field-battle rally waypoints Order_ToRallyWaypoint reads: two sides x two groups x three (x,y) int pairs, side 0 at 0x00522D30 and side 4 at 0x00522D60, group stride 0x18. Filled by Battlefield_BuildFromSkr and Battlefield_BuildRandom; on a .skr map all three of a group hold the same deployment marker cell.

globals.name: g_siegeApproachScore
globals.comment: Siege progress as the AI measures it, and the most-read global in the siege handlers. Raised by the routine that turns a filled-in moat cell into open ground - once per adjacent cell of surface 3, 4 or 5 - and by 4 when the drawbridge patch is laid. Thresholds used against it are 3, 4, 8, 10, 16 and 400. The name is a reading of what raises it, not a label from the binary.

globals.name: g_siegeBreachScore
globals.comment: Raised by the routine Missile_Step calls when a shot destroys a cell - once per orthogonal neighbour still of surface 5 - and by 4 when the drawbridge patch is laid. The siege-attacker handlers read non-zero as "there is a way in".

globals.name: g_attackersOnWall
globals.comment: Recounted every frame by Battle_UpdateAllMen: live figures of side 4 standing on a cell of surface 5. Every siege-defender handler branches on it, and at 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 attackers the defenders progressively abandon the wall for the keep.

globals.name: g_siegeEngineCount
globals.comment: Recounted every frame by Battle_UpdateAllMen: live figures of troop type 7, 8 or 9 - catapult, siege tower, battering ram - on either side. Three siege-attacker handlers refuse to move onto the castle objective while it is zero.

globals.name: g_formationTypePriority
globals.comment: Eleven ints indexed by troop type - 0, 4, 1, 2, 5, 3, 6, 10, 8, 9, 7 - the priority with which a troop type dictates its unit's formation geometry. Siege engines outrank everyone, then knights, pikemen, crossbowmen, archers, swordsmen, macemen, peasants.

globals.name: g_pathBlockedTemplate
globals.comment: The 80x80 u16 template Path_Search copies over g_pathCost before every search: 999 blocked, 0 free. Rebuilt by Path_BuildTerrainTemplate whenever the battlefield changes.

globals.name: g_pathFailCount
globals.comment: Zeroed by Battle_Start, incremented once per Path_Extract that returns no path. A ready-made diagnostic for how often the pathfinder is failing in a live battle.

globals.name: g_pathSearchCount
globals.comment: Zeroed by Battle_Start, incremented once per flood fill actually run - that is, excluding the adjacent and clear-line early outs.

globals.name: g_formationClaimedCells
globals.comment: A 100-entry list of cell byte offsets already claimed during one Formation_AssignSearchedSlots pass, so two figures of a unit are never sent to the same cell.

globals.name: g_scanBattleMan
globals.comment: Loop cursor of the figure-scanning target selectors - Missile_FindTarget and its two weighted variants, and Melee_ChooseChaseTarget - left holding the chosen figure on success.

globals.name: g_foundWallX
globals.comment: X of the cell Siege_FindCellSurface4 last returned.

globals.name: g_foundWallY
globals.comment: Y of the cell Siege_FindCellSurface4 last returned.

globals.name: g_formationFootprint
globals.comment: Cell footprint of the troop type Formation_PickGeometry chose for the current unit.

globals.name: g_formationCols
globals.comment: Figures per row of the current unit's formation rectangle, capped at the figure count and forced to 2 for units whose byte +0x09 is 1.

globals.name: g_formationOriginX
globals.comment: X of the top-left corner of the formation rectangle, and the output of Formation_FindNearbySlot.

globals.name: g_formationOriginY
globals.comment: Y of the top-left corner of the formation rectangle, and the output of Formation_FindNearbySlot.

globals.name: g_randStateA
globals.comment: First 31-bit LFSR state of Rand_Advance.

globals.name: g_randStateB
globals.comment: Second 31-bit LFSR state of Rand_Advance.

globals.name: g_rand7A
globals.comment: g_randStateA & 0x7F after Rand_Advance. Battle_UpdateStrengthAdvantage takes (value & 0x1F) - 10 from it, so the AI's read of its own strength wanders by -10..+21.

globals.name: g_deterministicBattle
globals.comment: Read by well over a hundred functions across the binary. Where it matters here: when it is zero Battle_Start picks g_battleApproachLane and g_battleRallyGroup at random and Battle_UpdateStrengthAdvantage adds its jitter; when it is non-zero both become deterministic cycles and the jitter is dropped. Sync_Checksum and Turn_AllRealmsDone also read it, and Troops_Load uses the side-neutral TROOPS.ENG when it is set. Everything is consistent with "this is a networked game, so nothing may diverge" - which is a reading, not a proof.

globals.name: g_moatFillSteps
globals.comment: Set to 15 by Rules_InitConstants. A figure filling in the moat (state 9) raises the target cell terrain byte by 1 every 81 frames - 101 if its owner is human - and the cell becomes open ground when the byte reaches this value.

globals.name: g_mapZoom
globals.comment: Campaign map zoom: 0 near (58x30 tiles) or 2 far (10x6). Written only by Map_SetZoom and Map_InitMode, and no caller ever passes 1, so the middle zoom is unreachable.

globals.name: g_mapScrollStep
globals.comment: Lattice columns per scroll step: 1 near, 4 far. Rows move by twice this, which keeps the origins parity.

globals.name: g_mapViewCols
globals.comment: Lattice columns visible: 8 near, 40 far. The lattice is 65 wide, so neither zoom shows the whole map.

globals.name: g_mapViewRows
globals.comment: Lattice rows visible: 30 near, 128 far. Map_RenderIso draws this many plus one, the first and last half-height.

globals.name: g_mapViewX
globals.comment: Left edge of the map viewport in screen pixels: 0 at both live zooms (4 at the dead middle one).

globals.name: g_mapViewY
globals.comment: Y of the first drawn lattice row: 9 near, 21 far. That row is top-clipped, so the visible band starts at viewY + rowStep = 24 at both zooms.

globals.name: g_mapTilePitch
globals.comment: Screen pixels between lattice columns: 60 near, 12 far - the tile frame width plus two.

globals.name: g_mapHalfPitch
globals.comment: Half the tile pitch: 30 near, 6 far.

globals.name: g_mapTileHalfStep
globals.comment: The same half pitch again, used as the x step for the half-offset lattice rows and as the divisor in Map_PickTile.

globals.name: g_mapRowStep
globals.comment: Screen pixels between lattice rows: 15 near, 3 far - half the tile frame height.

globals.name: g_mapViewRight
globals.comment: g_mapTilePitch * g_mapViewCols + g_mapViewX. 480 at all three zooms, which is what leaves 160 pixels for the right column.

globals.name: g_mapViewBottom
globals.comment: (g_mapViewRows + 1) * g_mapRowStep + g_mapViewY: 474 near, 408 far. Agrees with Map_PickTile s own bound and with Clip_Vertical(0x18, 0x1DA) in Map_DrawCountyFlag.

globals.name: g_mapStartCol
globals.comment: First visible lattice column, 0..64. Clamped by Map_ClampScroll.

globals.name: g_mapStartRow
globals.comment: First visible lattice row, 0..128, and always even - every setter uses an even literal, row & ~1, or steps of two.

globals.name: g_mapRotation
globals.comment: Map orientation, 0/2/4/6. Selects which of four projections Map_BuildLattice writes into g_screenLattice, and is subtracted from a unit facing to pick its sprite.

globals.name: g_mapScrollDir
globals.comment: Scroll direction 0..7 clockwise from north, 8 for none.

globals.name: g_optScrollSpeed
globals.comment: The Scroll Speed option, 0..100. Map_ScrollThrottle turns it into a minimum interval; 0 disables scrolling.

globals.name: g_drawX
globals.comment: Destination x for the next blit. The map render walk advances it by g_mapTilePitch per tile.

globals.name: g_drawY
globals.comment: Destination y for the next blit. The map render walk advances it by g_mapRowStep per lattice row.

globals.name: g_tileCursor
globals.comment: Byte offset into g_tiles of the tile the render walk is on, i.e. the lattice cell value. Values below 0x0FFF0000 are on-map.

globals.name: g_latticeRow
globals.comment: Lattice row cursor inside the render walk.

globals.name: g_latticeCol
globals.comment: Lattice column cursor inside the render walk.

globals.name: g_minimapPixels
globals.comment: The 128x128 minimap picture for the loaded slot, read straight out of MAPnn.PL8 by Minimap_Load. 0x4000 bytes, and 0x569590 + 0x4000 = 0x56D590, just below the render walks cursors.

globals.name: g_minimapCounty
globals.comment: The 128x128 county id per minimap pixel, the companion raster in MAPnn.PL8. Minimap_Click indexes it as g_minimapCounty[(x-480) + (y-25)*128].

globals.name: g_minimapMode
globals.comment: Minimap overlay: 0 owner colours, 1..3 three per-county ratings of the local players own counties.

globals.name: g_miscCtySheet
globals.comment: Misc_cty.pl8, loaded by Gfx_LoadCountyMode. Frames 54/55/56/57/58/59/66 are the 162-pixel-wide campaign right panel, 86..90 the realm banners, 91..95 the minimap furniture.

globals.name: g_panelsSheet
globals.comment: Panels.pl8, entry 10 of the startup preload table. 262 frames: two 52-frame 16x16 border sets at 0 and 204, a 144-frame 12x12 interior texture at 52, and eight 24x24 strip frames at 196.

globals.name: g_systemSheet
globals.comment: System2.pl8 or System.pl8, entry 9 of the preload table; swapped by name from the pair of strings at 0x004DBBD0.

globals.name: g_bankBase
globals.comment: Tile bank 0x00: Base1?.pl8 near, Base2?.pl8 far. Also the sheet the off-map surround is drawn from.

globals.name: g_bankMtns
globals.comment: Tile bank 0x04: Mtns1?.pl8 / Mtns2?.pl8.

globals.name: g_bankRoads
globals.comment: Tile bank 0x08: Roads1?.pl8 / Roads2?.pl8 - roads, woodland, fields and the county boundary frames.

globals.name: g_bankTown
globals.comment: Tile bank 0x0C: Town1?.pl8 / Town2?.pl8.

globals.name: g_bankCastle
globals.comment: Tile bank 0x10: Castle1?.pl8 / Castle2?.pl8. Never referenced by the stored map data, only by tiles the loader rewrites.

globals.name: g_spriteSheetA
globals.comment: Sprite1a.pl8 / Sprite2a.pl8 - armies on the campaign map.

globals.name: g_spriteSheetB
globals.comment: Sprite1b.pl8 / Sprite2b.pl8 - the second army sheet, selected by a unit type byte of 4.

globals.name: g_flagsSheet
globals.comment: Flags1a.pl8 / Flags2a.pl8 - the county flags drawn over castle tiles.

globals.name: g_preloadTable
globals.comment: 13 twenty-byte {char name[16]; u32 size;} records loaded once at startup: base01.256, t32_stn1.256, t32_bat1.256, fnt_8, fntl2_9, font_10, fntl2_14, fntl2_22, mouse, system2, panels, l2.eng, vill_gd8. It runs straight into g_resourceTable at 0x004DA050.

globals.name: g_paletteBase01
globals.comment: Base01.256, preload entry 0. Screen_DrawCampaign installs it, so this is the campaign screens palette.

globals.name: g_minimapRealmRamp
globals.comment: Eight bytes per realm colour; Minimap_DrawOverlay indexes realmColour*8 + (sourcePixel - 10) to shade county land on the minimap. The stride comes out of the index expression; the tables full extent is not otherwise pinned.

globals.name: g_minimapRatingRamp
globals.comment: Six bytes indexed by a 0..5 county rating for minimap overlay modes 1..3. Six because the code rejects values above 5.

globals.name: g_menuBarItems
globals.comment: Three 16-byte menu-bar records {x, measuredX, y, engGroup, ...}: (10, 6, group 1 File), (group 2 Options), (group 3 Help), each with its drop-down item count.

globals.name: g_countyTileTally
globals.comment: 32 dwords, one per county: how much of the viewport that county filled this frame. Map_DrawFrame seeds the current selection with 30 and then takes the maximum.

globals.name: g_overviewX
globals.comment: Left edge of the right-hand overview panel: 480.

globals.name: g_overviewY
globals.comment: Top of the overview panel: 48. Screen_HitRegion raises it to 24 in campaign mode.

globals.name: g_overviewW
globals.comment: Width of the overview panel: 160.

globals.name: g_overviewH
globals.comment: Height of the overview panel: 160.

globals.name: g_uiHotspotId
globals.comment: Id of the widget the pointer last acted on. For the minimap buttons 1..3 pick an overlay mode and 4 toggles the map zoom.

globals.name: g_screenHeight
globals.comment: 480. The vertical companion to g_screenStride, used as the bottom clip by every general blit.

globals.name: g_screenId
globals.comment: Which screen the interface is on. Screen_Draw, Screen_DrawWidgets and Screen_HandleInput all switch on it and nothing else does. The ids are listed in docs/screens-county.md section 1.

globals.name: g_setupPage
globals.comment: Sub-page within the game-setup screen (g_screenId 0x1F), 1..13.

globals.name: g_jobPanelJob
globals.comment: Which job the job popup is showing, 1..9 - the same index as L2.eng group 74, and one more than the labour slot.

globals.name: g_penAdvance
globals.comment: Width of the text drawn since the last reset, in pixels. Every panel zeroes it, draws a label, and adds it to the x of the value - which is how a label and its value are laid out without either knowing the other's width.

globals.name: g_uiHotspotArg
globals.comment: Widget record +0x14, published for the callback alongside g_uiHotspotId.

globals.name: g_villageDragCluster
globals.comment: The peasant cluster the rubber-band selection came from, 1-based; 0 for none.

globals.name: g_villageDragCount
globals.comment: How many peasant icons the rubber-band box selected. Multiplied by county +0xB8 to get workers.

globals.name: g_villageDropCluster
globals.comment: The cluster the drag was dropped on, 1-based.

globals.name: g_peasantIcons
globals.comment: Eight clusters of 25 bytes: the sprite frame plus one for each peasant icon on the village screen, or 0 for an empty slot. Rebuilt by Village_RebuildIcons.

globals.name: g_peasantIconSelected
globals.comment: 25 bytes, one per icon slot of the dragged cluster: 0 unselected, 1 or 2 for the two selected states.

globals.name: g_jobClusterOrigins
globals.comment: Eight {i32 x, i32 y} pairs - where each peasant cluster sits on the village, before the (0x40, g_villageTopY) offset: (22,50) (147,30) (271,26) (268,188) (117,200) (15,245) (146,120) (19,122).

globals.name: g_peasantIconOffsets
globals.comment: 25 {u8 x, u8 y} pairs - a 5x5 grid 16 pixels apart in x and 12 in y, with the rows staggered 0, 4, 8, 0, 4. Twenty-five slots because one icon is one twenty-fifth of the county.

globals.name: g_jobClusterToSlot
globals.comment: Eight i32: which labour slot each village cluster is. [5, 0, 1, 3, 6, 7, 8, 2], with cluster 0 overridden to 4 by Job_SlotForCluster.

globals.name: g_taxHappinessOther
globals.comment: i32 by tax rate: the "Other counties" happiness term (county +0x16) that Tax_RecomputePreview writes. 0 up to rate 19, then -1 at 20 falling to -15 at 50. Exactly 51 entries, which is a second reading of the 0..50 tax ceiling.

globals.name: g_countyHistory
globals.comment: 400 turns x 16 counties x 8 bytes: population as u32 at +0x00 and happiness as u8 at +0x04, indexed by county - 1. What both graph panels draw. g_saveBlocks block 10 is exactly {0x0056D8C0, 51200}, and the shipped lastturn.sav reads back all fourteen counties' stored population and happiness at turn 0.

globals.name: g_historyHead
globals.comment: Write cursor into g_countyHistory, wrapping at 400.

globals.name: g_historyLength
globals.comment: How many turns of g_countyHistory are filled, and how many bars Ui_HistoryGraph draws.

globals.name: g_taxWidgets
globals.comment: Two 24-byte widget records: the tax panel's up arrow at (192,162) frame 0x15 and its down arrow at (224,162) frame 0x17, both 24x24, kind 4.

globals.name: g_rationWidgets
globals.comment: Two 24-byte widget records: the ration panel's arrows at (344,130) and (368,130), frames 0x15 and 0x17.

globals.name: g_sidebarButtons
globals.comment: Six hotspot records for the map sidebar, offset by (478, 430): five 32-pixel buttons across the 162x30 strip, then the full-width end-turn button below it.

globals.name: g_minimapModeButtons
globals.comment: Four hotspot records at (610, 32), a vertical column inside the sidebar's top plate.

globals.name: g_fontHeading
globals.comment: Fntl2_22.pl8 - every panel heading.

globals.name: g_fontBody
globals.comment: Fntl2_14.pl8 - every panel body line.

globals.name: g_fontSmall
globals.comment: Fntl2_9.pl8 - the county strip, and nothing else.

globals.name: g_font10
globals.comment: Font_10.pl8.

globals.name: g_font8
globals.comment: Fnt_8.pl8 - the battle overlay.

globals.name: g_mouseSheet
globals.comment: mouse.pl8 - the pointer.

globals.name: g_engText
globals.comment: l2.eng, whole. Eng_GroupBase indexes the group table from here.

globals.name: g_numberBuffer
globals.comment: 100-byte scratch that Ui_NumberToBuffer formats into and Ui_DrawNumber draws from.

globals.name: g_playerNames
globals.comment: Six 0x2C-byte player names. g_saveBlocks entry 2 is {0x00553D50, 264}, which is 6 x 0x2C.

globals.name: g_villageTopY
globals.comment: Where the village scene starts: 64 normally, 132 with Advanced Farming, which is the strip the fertility and weather lines occupy.

globals.name: g_glyphWidths
globals.comment: One byte per printable character; zero means a four-pixel blank, which is what makes '@' an invisible sign column.
